Title:
linkedin_oidc provider uses api.linkedin.com for the authorization redirect instead of LinkedIn's documented www.linkedin.com, breaking session recognition and forcing password re-entry on every sign-in

Body:

Summary

The linkedin_oidc OAuth provider builds its authorization URL against https://api.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization. LinkedIn's own developer documentation specifies the interactive authorization endpoint as https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization. As a result, users with an active, valid linkedin.com browser session are not recognized when authorizing through Supabase, and LinkedIn falls back to a full username/password login screen (/uas/login) on every single sign-in attempt — even immediately after a successful one. Sites that call LinkedIn's documented www.linkedin.com endpoint directly do not have this problem; they get LinkedIn's normal "Continue as [Name]" session-based consent screen.

Environment
Provider: linkedin_oidc ("LinkedIn (OIDC)" in the Supabase Dashboard)
Client library: supabase-js signInWithOAuth({ provider: "linkedin_oidc" })
Hosted Supabase project (not self-hosted)
Steps to reproduce
Enable the LinkedIn (OIDC) provider in a Supabase project with a valid LinkedIn app (Client ID/Secret).
Call supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({ provider: "linkedin_oidc", options: { redirectTo } }) from a browser that already has an active linkedin.com session (i.e., the user is logged into linkedin.com in that same browser).
Observe the resulting redirect chain in the browser's Network tab.
Actual behavior

The request chain is:

https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/authorize?provider=linkedin_oidc&...&code_challenge_method=s256
  → https://api.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization?client_id=...&redirect_uri=https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback&response_type=code&scope=openid+email+profile&state=...
  → https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=...   ← forces full login/password screen, every time
Expected behavior

Per LinkedIn's documentation, the authorization request should go to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization. When it does (verified against a separate, unrelated third-party app in the same browser, at the same time, with the same LinkedIn session), LinkedIn correctly recognizes the existing session and presents its normal "Continue as [Name]" consent screen — no password re-entry.

Root cause

In internal/api/provider/linkedin_oidc.go:

go
const (
	defaultLinkedinOIDCAPIBase = "api.linkedin.com"
	IssuerLinkedin             = "https://www.linkedin.com/oauth"
)
...
apiPath := chooseHost(ext.URL, defaultLinkedinOIDCAPIBase)
...
Endpoint: oauth2.Endpoint{
    AuthURL:  apiPath + "/oauth/v2/authorization",
    TokenURL: apiPath + "/oauth/v2/accessToken",
},

api.linkedin.com is LinkedIn's REST API host (used for calls like api.linkedin.com/v2/me after a token is issued), not the documented interactive OAuth authorization host. The IssuerLinkedin constant in the same file already correctly uses www.linkedin.com for OIDC token/issuer validation — only the interactive AuthURL (and TokenURL) default is wrong. The same incorrect default also exists in the legacy internal/api/provider/linkedin.go provider (defaultLinkedinAPIBase = "api.linkedin.com").

Suggested fix

Change defaultLinkedinOIDCAPIBase (and the legacy defaultLinkedinAPIBase) to www.linkedin.com, matching LinkedIn's documented authorization endpoint (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/authentication/authorization-code-flow) and the IssuerLinkedin constant already used elsewhere in the same file.

Impact

Every hosted Supabase project using the built-in LinkedIn (OIDC) provider forces users to re-enter their LinkedIn password on every sign-in, with no session persistence — regardless of whether the user is already logged into linkedin.com. There is currently no dashboard setting or documented override to correct the host from the client side.
items.title: linkedin_oidc provider uses api.linkedin.com for the authorization redirect instead of www.linkedin.com

## Summary

On a hosted Supabase project, **every nested insert** (parent + child in one
request) is rejected by PostgREST with `PGRST204`, even though the foreign key
exists and is validated, read embeds on the same relationship work, and both the
parent and child can be inserted separately.

This is project-wide: it reproduces on our own tables **and** on a freshly created
parent/child pair.

## Environment

- Supabase hosted project ref: `houuewkkodsfayinbbao`
- PostgREST reported by the error path: **14.5**
- Region: (fill in if relevant)
- Client: `@supabase/supabase-js` via PostgREST over HTTPS

## Steps to reproduce

Two tables in `public` with a normal, validated FK:

```sql
create table parent_probe (id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(), name text not null);
create table child_probe (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  parent_id uuid not null references parent_probe(id) on delete cascade,
  name text not null
);
```

Then, authenticated with a valid user JWT whose RLS grants insert on both tables:

```bash
# 1. Plain parent insert -> works
curl -X POST "$URL/rest/v1/parent_probe" \
  -H "apikey: $PUBLISHABLE" -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Prefer: return=representation" \
  -d '{"name":"p"}'
# 201 Created

# 2. Nested insert -> fails
curl -X POST "$URL/rest/v1/parent_probe" \
  -H "apikey: $PUBLISHABLE" -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Prefer: return=representation" \
  -d '{"name":"p","child_probe":[{"name":"c"}]}'
# 400 Bad Request
# {"code":"PGRST204","details":null,"hint":null,
#  "message":"Could not find the 'child_probe' column of 'parent_probe' in the schema cache"}
```

## Expected

The nested insert creates the parent and its children in one transaction, exactly
like the equivalent **read** embed resolves the relationship.

## Actual

PostgREST treats the embedded resource name as a *column* of the parent table and
returns `PGRST204`.

## Evidence

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| FK exists and is validated (`pg_constraint`, `convalidated = true`) | ✅ |
| Read embed `GET /parent_probe?select=id,child_probe(id)` | ✅ `200`, children returned |
| Plain parent insert | ✅ `201` |
| Direct child insert | ✅ `201` |
| **Nested insert (parent + children)** | ❌ `400 PGRST204` |
| Same nested insert on a freshly created pair | ❌ `400 PGRST204` |

Real-world tables show the same behaviour (`workouts` + `workout_exercises`,
`groups` + `group_members`, `tenants` + `tenant_modules`), so it is not specific to
one schema.

## What we tried (none of it helped)

- `notify pgrst, 'reload schema'`
- `notify pgrst, 'reload config'`
- `notify pgrst, 'reload tables'`
- `notify pgrst, 'reload relationships'`
- Re-adding the foreign key constraint
- **Restarting the project's Data API** (toggling it off/on)
- `pg_notification_queue_usage()` returns `0`

The schema cache is otherwise provably fresh: a new table `COMMENT` shows up in
`GET /rest/v1/` immediately, and read embeds on the same relationship resolve
correctly. The FK relationship is therefore known to PostgREST for reads but not
for writes.

## Impact

**Nested inserts are completely unusable on this project.** Any application that
creates a parent with its children in one request is broken — in our case it means
workouts can never be created. The workaround is an RPC that performs both inserts
inside one SQL function, which we have adopted, but the PostgREST behaviour still
looks incorrect.

## Additional context

This matches other reports of schema-cache/relationship corruption on specific
projects (e.g. supabase/supabase#42183, supabase/supabase#39446), where the
documented remedy — restarting the Data API — also did not resolve it.

If it helps, we can grant temporary read access to the project for triage.
items.title: Nested inserts fail with `PGRST204 Could not find the '<child table>' column` while read embeds and plain inserts succeed

## Describe the problem
Supabase Dashboard repeatedly returns to the sign-in page after authentication with either GitHub or ChatGPT in the Codex desktop in-app browser on Windows. This is blocking our project development and administration in this environment. The root cause is unknown; this may be an embedded-browser compatibility or session-handling issue. We are not reporting a confirmed database outage.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open https://supabase.com/dashboard/sign-in in the Codex in-app browser.
2. Select Continue with GitHub (GitHub itself is already signed in and remains accessible), or Continue with ChatGPT and select the existing account.
3. The browser returns to Supabase and briefly reaches /dashboard/sign-in-mfa; in some attempts a dashboard/project loading view also appears briefly.
4. Within seconds, it returns to /dashboard/sign-in instead of maintaining an authenticated dashboard session. No actionable error or stable MFA-entry screen is shown during these OAuth attempts.
5. Repeating the flow does not resolve the issue.

## Expected behavior
Complete the existing account sign-in, show an actionable MFA challenge if required, and keep the authenticated dashboard session active.

## Impact and troubleshooting
- Project administration and SQL Editor work are blocked in the affected environment.
- Retested after closing/reopening the app and opening fresh tabs; the loop persists.
- Both GitHub and ChatGPT sign-in paths were tested.
- GitHub stays signed in in the same browser.
- The account owner reports that Supabase can remain signed in in standalone Chrome; that comparison has not been independently verified in this session.
- The official Open support ticket link at https://supabase.com/dashboard/support/new also redirects to sign-in, preventing a private ticket from being submitted through that route.

## Environment
- Windows desktop
- Codex desktop in-app browser (exact app/browser build not collected)
- Hosted Supabase Dashboard, not self-hosted Studio
- Reproduced on 23 September 2026

## Requested help
Please triage this blocking dashboard access problem and advise on a supported workaround or a private support channel that does not require a functioning dashboard login. Please indicate whether the OAuth-to-MFA transition or embedded-browser session handling could explain this behavior.

No credentials, authentication tokens, account email, project identifiers, or customer data are included in this public report.

## Summary

Every Copy button in Studio fails in Safari with the toast **"Unable to copy to clipboard"**. On the affected Safari, `navigator.clipboard.write()` rejects with `NotAllowedError` while `navigator.clipboard.writeText()` works normally. Studio has at least two independent copy paths and both commit to `write()` without ever falling back to `writeText()`.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Browser | Safari 27.0 |
| OS | macOS 26 (build 26A428), Apple Silicon |
| Studio commit | `05a45dd1edbaeb972d960e181b18cb4878b49674` (2026-09-22T22:52:07Z) |
| Safari extensions | none enabled |
| Lockdown Mode | off |
| Chrome, same machine | works |
| Other sites in Safari (GitHub copy buttons) | work — they use `writeText()` |

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Safari.
2. Go to Project Settings → API Keys → **Legacy anon, service_role API keys**.
3. Click any **Copy** button.

**Expected:** key is copied.
**Actual:** toast "Unable to copy to clipboard". Nothing reaches the clipboard.

```
NotAllowedError: The request is not allowed by the user agent or the platform in the current context,
possibly because the user denied permission.
write
(anonymous function) — 1hdqq-u-k_pkz.js:10:21436
onClick — 1hdqq-u-k_pkz.js:10:7873
```

Clicking directly on the key field (instead of the Copy button) produces a second, different stack — from Studio's Monaco/VS Code-derived clipboard service:

```
Unhandled Promise Rejection: Canceled: Canceled
  (anonymous function) — async.ts:744
  Promise
  error — async.ts:743
  g — clipboardService.ts:68

ERR
NotAllowedError: The request is not allowed by the user agent or the platform in the current context,
possibly because the user denied permission.
  write
  g — clipboardService.ts:76
```

Two independent copy paths, different code, same failure: both call `navigator.clipboard.write()`, neither falls back to `writeText()`.

## The user's machine is not the problem

Ruled out with an `NSPasteboard.changeCount` monitor running on the affected Mac while the user reproduced the bug. Every line below is a real clipboard write captured live:

```
[21:07:56] 7->8   Safari  164 chars  webarchive/rtf          <- Cmd+C on an unrelated page: works
[21:08:52] 8->9   Safari  211 chars  public.utf8-plain-text  <- Cmd+C on text FROM THIS SAME PAGE: works
[21:09:23] 9->10  Safari  (no text)  public.png              <- screenshot to clipboard: works
```

Between 21:08:52 and 21:09:23 the user clicked the key field and pressed Cmd+C: **no pasteboard write was recorded at all.**

So on this machine the system pasteboard is healthy, Safari's native Cmd+C works, it works on the very page that fails, and images copy fine. Also ruled out: Lockdown Mode (off), Safari extensions (none), per-site clipboard settings (none), managed policies (none), and any other process contending for the pasteboard (a separate 20s monitor recorded zero spontaneous writes).

The only thing that fails is Studio's own copy paths.

## Minimal reproduction

Paste into the Safari console on any Studio page, then click each button **separately** (WebKit allows one clipboard write per user gesture):

```js
[['A writeText','#c00',()=>navigator.clipboard.writeText('A')],
 ['B Blob direct','#070',()=>navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'text/plain':new Blob(['B'],{type:'text/plain'})})])],
 ['C Blob in promise','#00c',()=>navigator.clipboard.write([new ClipboardItem({'text/plain':Promise.resolve('C').then(t=>new Blob([t],{type:'text/plain'}))})])]
].forEach(([n,bg,fn],i)=>{const b=document.createElement('button');b.textContent=n;
b.style.cssText=`position:fixed;z-index:99999;top:${10+i*44}px;left:10px;padding:10px 16px;background:${bg};color:#fff;font-size:15px;border:0;border-radius:6px`;
b.onclick=async()=>{try{await fn();console.log('OK '+n)}catch(e){console.log('FAIL '+n+': '+e.name+' — '+e.message)}};
document.body.appendChild(b)});
```

Results on the affected machine:

| Variant | API | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | `navigator.clipboard.writeText(str)` | **OK** |
| B | `navigator.clipboard.write([ClipboardItem])`, Blob passed directly | **NotAllowedError** |
| C | `navigator.clipboard.write([ClipboardItem])`, Blob wrapped in a Promise | **NotAllowedError** |

Each button is freshly created, has a direct `onclick`, and performs exactly one clipboard write per gesture. So this is not lost user activation, and not the promise wrapper. `navigator.clipboard.write()` itself is rejected by this Safari; `writeText()` is not.

## Root cause

`packages/ui/src/lib/utils/clipboard.ts` (identical on `master` and on the deployed commit):

```ts
try {
  if (typeof ClipboardItem !== 'undefined' && navigator.clipboard?.write) {
    const text = new ClipboardItem({
      'text/plain': Promise.resolve(str).then((text) => new Blob([text], { type: 'text/plain' })),
    })

    await navigator.clipboard.write([text])
    callback()
    return
  }

  if (!navigator.clipboard) throw new Error('Clipboard API unavailable')

  await Promise.resolve(str).then((text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text))
  callback()
} catch {
  toast.error('Unable to copy to clipboard')
}
```

The branch is chosen by whether `navigator.clipboard.write` **exists**, not by whether it **works**. Safari exposes it, so the `write` path is always taken there, and the early `return` makes the `writeText` path below dead code for Safari. When `write()` rejects, control goes straight to the `catch` and the user gets the toast — even though `writeText()` succeeds on the same page, in the same gesture.

The `write([ClipboardItem])` path exists to support `Promise<string>` inputs in Safari, per the comments in the file. That need is real. The bug is that the path has no fallback.

## Suggested fix

```ts
try {
  if (typeof ClipboardItem !== 'undefined' && navigator.clipboard?.write) {
    try {
      const text = new ClipboardItem({
        'text/plain': Promise.resolve(str).then((text) => new Blob([text], { type: 'text/plain' })),
      })
      await navigator.clipboard.write([text])
      callback()
      return
    } catch {
      // Safari can expose clipboard.write() and still reject it. Fall through to writeText().
    }
  }

  if (!navigator.clipboard) throw new Error('Clipboard API unavailable')

  await Promise.resolve(str).then((text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text))
  callback()
} catch {
  toast.error('Unable to copy to clipboard')
}
```

Note on the Safari caveat documented in the file: awaiting the `str` promise before `writeText()` can lose user activation in Safari. That only matters for callers passing a `Promise<string>`. For a plain string — which is what `ui-patterns/src/DataInputs/Input.tsx` passes via `_onCopy` for every Copy button in Studio — `Promise.resolve(str)` settles in a microtask within the same task, so activation is intact. If the distinction matters, gate the fallback on `typeof str === 'string'`.

The Monaco-derived path behind `clipboardService.ts` needs the same treatment.

## Secondary finding: Safari AutoFill-generated passwords cannot be copied either

Separate mechanism, same user-visible symptom, different dialog.

On **Database → Settings → Reset database password**:

- Password generated by **Safari's own strong-password AutoFill** → Copy fails with the same `NotAllowedError` / `clipboardService.ts:76` stack.
- Password generated by Supabase's own **"Generate a password"** link → Copy works.

Likely cause: WebKit withholds AutoFilled password-field values from page JavaScript until the user manually interacts with the field — an anti-exfiltration protection. Studio's copy handler reads `input.value`, gets nothing usable, and the clipboard call fails. When Studio itself sets the value, there is no AutoFill protection and the copy succeeds.

Worth handling explicitly: if the value read back from a password field is empty or the clipboard write fails, the UI should say so rather than emitting a generic "Unable to copy to clipboard", since the user can see a filled field and has no way to guess why.

## Not investigated

Why this Safari rejects `navigator.clipboard.write()` at all. That is a WebKit question, possibly specific to Safari 27 / macOS 26. Worth filing separately with Apple. The Studio-side fix is independent of the answer: any `write()` failure, from any cause, should degrade to `writeText()` rather than to an error toast.
items.title: Copy buttons fail in Safari: Studio calls navigator.clipboard.write() with no fallback to writeText()

### Summary

Server-side REST requests authenticated with the **new-format `sb_secret_` API key** intermittently fail with:

```
HTTP 401
PGRST303 — JWT issued at future
```

We never mint or send a JWT. The token being validated is created **inside Supabase** (the gateway exchanges the opaque `sb_secret_` key for a short-lived JWT before forwarding to PostgREST), so the `iat` being "in the future" can only mean clock skew between two Supabase components.

This has been reported twice before and both were closed as `awaiting-details`:

- supabase/supabase#49655 — same key format, same error
- supabase/supabase#41294 — more severe variant (PostgREST ~15h ahead)

This report adds the details those were missing: a **19-day timeline**, **HTTP-level evidence**, and a measurement showing the skew **sometimes exceeds 2 seconds**.

---

### What we send

| | |
|---|---|
| Client | `@supabase/supabase-js`, server-side (Node 26) |
| Auth | `sb_secret_…` key (new format, **not** a legacy JWT service key) |
| Token minted by us | **none** |
| Our host | Railway; our own clock shows no skew in our logs |

The key format carries no `iat` claim, so the rejected timestamp cannot be one we supplied.

---

### Timeline (all UTC)

**2026-09-02** — 5 × HTTP 500 out of 501 requests over a 5-hour window, across three different public pages. Several independent server-side reads (settings, regions, payment methods, one product table) all failed in the **same second** with the identical message. One failure was reproduced in a browser; the Next.js error digest shown to the visitor matched the server log exactly.

**2026-09-19 21:03:30** — public page → 500. Failing read was a `select` with an `!inner` join. Supabase returned **401 / PGRST303**.

**2026-09-20 11:12:29** — different public page → 500. Failing read was a simple single-table `select`. Same 401 / PGRST303.

Between those dates the error appeared only intermittently; it is not reproducible on demand, which is why this is a measurement report rather than a repro script.

---

### Sizing the skew

After the 2026-09-02 event we added a fetch-level retry that fires only on `401/403` **and** this specific body signature:

| | |
|---|---|
| Attempts | 4 |
| Backoff | 120 ms, 320 ms, 600 ms, 1000 ms (~2 s total budget) |

In one 11-minute window we observed **two** occurrences: one recovered inside the ~2 s budget, the other did **not**.

That is the part we think is new: #49655 reported recovery at ~1.4 s, which suggests sub-second skew. **We have at least one occurrence where the skew outlived a 2-second retry budget.**

---

### Impact

Public, crawlable pages returned HTTP 500 to real visitors and to search-engine crawlers. The failure is transient and unpredictable, so it is invisible to uptime checks that sample infrequently.

---

### Questions

1. Can you confirm whether NTP skew between the API gateway and PostgREST is known on the affected instances, and whether there is a fix in progress?
2. `PGRST303` says "JWT issued at future" even when the caller supplied a **non-JWT** `sb_secret_` key. Could the message distinguish *gateway-minted* tokens from caller-supplied ones? Right now users cannot tell "your clock" from "our clock", which is likely why the earlier reports were closed as external.
3. Is there a supported client-side leeway/tolerance setting, or is retrying the only mitigation available to users?

---

### Mitigations we shipped (context, not a fix request)

- Fetch-level retry on this exact signature (above)
- Config reads fall back to the last known-good snapshot for up to 5 minutes
- One cached page serves its existing snapshot instead of a 500 when this specific error occurs

None address the cause. Happy to supply request IDs and exact timestamps privately for a specific project ref if that helps.
items.title: PGRST303 "JWT issued at future" with sb_secret_ keys — skew sometimes exceeds a 2s retry budget (adds details to #49655)

# Bug report

We've had recurring production outages on this project caused by the transaction pooler (port 6543) intermittently hanging on requests, even for trivial, fast, indexed queries. The direct/session pooler (port 5432) has never once failed under the same conditions.

Timeline:

Started ~2026-09-20 01:00 UTC: intermittent canceling statement due to statement timeout (57014) errors on the transaction pooler, alongside repeated schema "pg_pgrst_no_exposed_schemas" does not exist PostgREST errors logged every ~30s.
We restarted the project (01:23:54 UTC) — did not resolve it.
We upgraded Postgres from 17.6.1.155 to 17.6.1.166 (~02:04-02:1x UTC) — PostgREST errors stopped, but the transaction pooler kept hanging.
Reproduced directly: a SELECT created_at FROM users WHERE ... query (12 rows, indexed, runs in ~230ms via direct/session connection) sat in pg_stat_activity as state=active, wait_event_type=Client, wait_event=ClientRead for 5+ minutes when issued through the transaction pooler, until the calling app's request timed out (300s) with no error ever returned to the client — the connection just never released.
The exact same query pattern via the port-5432 pooler has been 100% reliable across dozens of tests over 2+ hours.

items.body:
## Page

https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/broadcast#broadcast-from-the-database

Source: `apps/docs/content/guides/realtime/broadcast.mdx`

## Problem

The `private` argument gets three different labels on this page, and two of them are reversed:

- `realtime.send` example: `false -- Public / Private flag`
- `realtime.send_binary` example: `true -- Private / Public flag (defaults to true)`
- "Broadcasting a message from your database" section: `FALSE -- Public / Private flag`

None of them say what `true` and `false` do. `private` is a positional boolean, so a wrong value changes whether the message needs channel authorization, and a public message never reaches a private channel.

The note near the top of the page also calls it "the public flag" while the parameter is named `private`:

> The public flag (the last argument in `realtime.send(payload, event, topic, is_private)`) only affects who can subscribe to the topic not who can read messages from the database.

That note explains the values correctly. The inline comments in the examples contradict it.

## Ground truth

Both functions declare the argument the same way:

```sql
create or replace function realtime.send (
  payload jsonb,
  event   text,
  topic   text,
  private boolean default true
)
```

`private => true` sends on a private channel. `private => false` sends on a public channel. The default is `true`.

## Fix

- Use one label for the parameter in all three SQL examples.
- State what the values do, for example `-- private: true = private channel (default), false = public channel`.
- Show the `true` default in the `realtime.send` example too.
- Call it "the `private` flag" in the note, to match the parameter name.
- Consider [named notation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-syntax-calling-funcs.html#SQL-SYNTAX-CALLING-FUNCS-NAMED) in the examples, so the call documents itself:

```sql
select realtime.send(
  payload => jsonb_build_object('hello', 'world'),
  event   => 'event',
  topic   => 'topic',
  private => true
);
```

Ref REAL-1051

3. Move the mouse away (or press Esc) so the dropdown closes.
4. Try to select the hero heading text, or click **"Start your project"**.

I was setting up a self-hosted instance and wanted to use a custom database name instead of the default `postgres`. After changing `POSTGRES_DB` in my `.env` file, I noticed that auth and RLS weren't working correctly.

```sql
Expected behavior
jwt.sql should read the POSTGRES_DB environment variable and apply the settings to that database.
```

Change POSTGRES_DB=custom_db in .env.
Run docker compose up -d.
Check custom_db for app.settings.jwt_exp — it will be missing because it was applied to postgres instead.

# Bug report

- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application.
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com).

## Describe the bug

Studio's **Exposed functions** state can report a function as `revoked` even though `anon` can still execute it through PostgreSQL's `PUBLIC EXECUTE` privilege.

I reproduced the mismatch end-to-end with PostgREST:

```text
Studio access state:
  anon_execute = false
  status = revoked

PostgreSQL effective privilege:
  has_function_privilege('anon', function_oid, 'EXECUTE') = true

PostgREST:
  POST /rest/v1/rpc/<function>
  → HTTP 200
  → current_user = anon
```

So the access state shown by Studio can disagree with the privilege PostgreSQL/PostgREST actually enforces.

## To Reproduce

This reproduces with the current default-privilege behavior used by Studio.

1. Create a function without an explicit ACL:

```sql
create function public.studio_privilege_repro()
returns json
language sql
as $$
  select json_build_object(
    'ok', true,
    'current_user', current_user
  );
$$;
```

2. Check the effective privilege:

```sql
select has_function_privilege(
  'anon',
  'public.studio_privilege_repro()',
  'EXECUTE'
);
```

This returns `true`. `proacl` is `NULL`, so PostgreSQL falls back to its built-in function ACL, which grants `EXECUTE` to `PUBLIC`.

3. Check Studio's Exposed functions state for the same function. The query reports:

```text
anon_execute = false
auth_execute = false
srv_execute = false
status = revoked
```

4. Call the function through PostgREST as the anonymous role:

```text
POST /rest/v1/rpc/studio_privilege_repro
```

Result:

```text
HTTP 200

{
  "ok": true,
  "current_user": "anon"
}
```

The RPC also appears in PostgREST's OpenAPI output.

## Expected behavior

Studio's **Exposed functions** state should reflect whether the Data API roles can effectively execute a function.

If `anon` can invoke the function through the Data API, Studio should not classify it as `revoked` for `anon`.

## Screenshots

Not applicable. This was reproduced from the Studio SQL used by Exposed functions plus a PostgREST RPC, not from a Dashboard screenshot.

## System information

- OS: Linux (WSL2)
- Browser (if applies): N/A (not reproduced through the Studio UI)
- Version of supabase-js: N/A
- Version of Node.js: N/A
- PostgreSQL: 16.15
- PostgREST: 16.1
- Supabase: current `master`

## Additional context

Studio derives function access from the explicit ACL using roughly:

```text
aclexplode(...)
→ grantee
→ pg_roles
```

PostgreSQL represents the `PUBLIC` ACL entry with grantee OID `0`, and `PUBLIC` is not a row in `pg_roles`.

As a result, access inherited through `PUBLIC` is not attributed to `anon`, `authenticated`, or `service_role`, even though PostgreSQL considers those roles able to execute the function.

For comparison:

```sql
select has_function_privilege(
  'anon',
  function_oid,
  'EXECUTE'
);
```

does account for effective privileges, including access through `PUBLIC`.

After explicitly revoking execution from `PUBLIC`:

```sql
revoke execute
on function public.studio_privilege_repro()
from public, anon, authenticated;
```

the result changes to:

```text
has_function_privilege = false
proacl = {postgres=X/postgres}

POST /rest/v1/rpc/studio_privilege_repro
→ HTTP 401
→ 42501: permission denied for function studio_privilege_repro
```

So the successful request above is caused by the effective PostgreSQL privilege, not by PostgREST bypassing function permissions.

The underlying PostgreSQL default-privilege behavior is already discussed elsewhere:

- #43884 — unexpected default `EXECUTE` privileges on functions
- #49338 — ineffective schema-scoped `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC` in the hardening docs
- #49366 — docs fix; also notes that Studio generates the same schema-scoped revoke but intentionally leaves that product behavior out of scope
- Discussion #45329 — broader discussion around automatic Data API privileges

This issue is intentionally narrower.

It is **not** proposing whether Supabase should globally revoke PostgreSQL's built-in `PUBLIC EXECUTE` privilege.

The issue here is that Studio reports the function as revoked / not exposed while the Data API role can effectively execute it.

No production or existing project database was used.
items.title: [Studio] Functions can be shown as revoked while remaining executable through PUBLIC

I searched the Supabase documentation and existing GitHub issues. The closest existing report is supabase/supavisor#1061, with fixes merged in supabase/supavisor#1079 and the follow-up supabase/supavisor#1176.

## Describe the bug

The hosted Supabase transaction pooler on port 6543 still reproduced the dropped-reply/hanging-client behavior described in supabase/supavisor#1061.

A postgres.js 3.4.7 client using `prepare: false` and `max_pipeline: 1` sent another extended-query batch before receiving `ReadyForQuery` for the preceding batch. In the captured failing run, the frontend sent 11 Parse/Describe sequences, but only 10 corresponding ParseComplete/ParameterDescription replies returned. The outstanding postgres.js promise then waited indefinitely.

This appears consistent with the backend being released after an earlier `ReadyForQuery` while replies from a later pipelined batch are still outstanding—the behavior addressed by supabase/supavisor#1079 and supabase/supavisor#1176.

This affected ordinary read-only application queries. Prepared statements were disabled.

## To Reproduce

Client shape:

```js
import postgres from 'postgres'

const sql = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL, {
  max: 1,
  prepare: false,
  ssl: 'require',
  max_pipeline: 1,
})

// Six independent read-only SELECTs are started concurrently by one loader.
await Promise.all([read1(sql), read2(sql), read3(sql), read4(sql), read5(sql), read6(sql)])
```

1. Use the hosted transaction-pooler connection string on port 6543.
2. Run six distinct unprepared read-only queries concurrently on one postgres.js connection.
3. Repeat the loader call. Our incident harness used 20 uncached calls with a 12-second deadline.
4. Trace frontend Parse/Describe/Sync and backend ParseComplete/ParameterDescription/ReadyForQuery messages.
5. With `max_pipeline: 1`, we captured a missing reply and a permanently unresolved client promise.

Our public application workaround and regression harness are in alanxchen85/gradschooldb#1581:

- PR: https://github.com/alanxchen85/gradschooldb/pull/1581
- Live hosted-pooler trace gate: https://github.com/alanxchen85/gradschooldb/blob/e167349d51bb53390d457393e712cfe273580775/tests/regression/pooler/live/transaction-fanout.repro.ts
- Gate documentation: https://github.com/alanxchen85/gradschooldb/blob/e167349d51bb53390d457393e712cfe273580775/tests/regression/pooler/README.md

The deterministic local gate has a `max_pipeline: 1` canary that strands and records the dropped frame. The hosted acceptance gate verifies the workaround at client pool sizes 1 and 5.

## Expected behavior

The hosted transaction pooler should retain the backend until every expected `ReadyForQuery` has arrived and return every reply to the client. Concurrent ordinary queries should either complete or fail explicitly; they should not leave a postgres.js promise unresolved.

## Screenshots

Not applicable. The useful evidence is the PostgreSQL protocol trace and the linked executable regression harness.

## System information

- Client OS: macOS
- Deployment environment affected: Vercel Linux functions/builds
- Client library: postgres.js 3.4.7
- Node.js: 22.22.3
- Supabase connection: hosted shared transaction pooler, port 6543
- Client options: `prepare: false`, TLS required

## Additional context

Our current client-side workaround disables postgres.js pipelining with `max_pipeline: 0`. Because postgres.js 3.4.7 does not run the `sql.begin()` reservation hook correctly at that limit, our application also carries a small ordering patch. With that workaround:

- pool size 1: 20 loader calls x 6 queries = 120/120 completed
- pool size 5: 20 loader calls x 6 queries = 120/120 completed
- zero hangs, zero dropped replies, balanced protocol counters
- p95 below 3 seconds in both hosted-pooler acceptance runs

We are not proposing that client patch as the Supabase fix. We would like to establish whether the hosted service has received the existing Supavisor fixes.

Could Supabase confirm:

1. Which Supavisor version is currently deployed to hosted shared transaction poolers?
2. Does the hosted deployment include supabase/supavisor#1079 and supabase/supavisor#1176?
3. If not, what is the rollout timeline?
4. If those fixes are already deployed, what additional tenant/region and packet-trace information should we provide privately to support?

We can share the affected project and region privately with Supabase staff, but have intentionally omitted tenant identifiers and connection details from this public report.

# Improve documentation

## Link

- https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-diff-a-branch
- https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-list-all-branches
- Source spec: `https://api.supabase.com/api/v1-json`

## Describe the problem

Two gaps in how the Branching surface of the Management API is described. Both come
from the OpenAPI spec that generates these reference pages, so they show up both in
the docs and in every client generated from the spec.

Filing together because they share a namespace (happy to split if you'd prefer).

### 1. Every branching endpoint documents `500` and nothing else — except one

Across the whole v1 spec, **151 of 169 operations** document `401`, `403` and `429`.
Inside the branching namespace that ratio inverts:

| Method | Path | Documented error responses |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}` | `500` |
| PATCH | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}` | `500` |
| DELETE | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}` | `500` |
| GET | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/diff` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/merge` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/push` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/reset` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/restore` | `500` |
| GET | `/v1/projects/{ref}/branches` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/projects/{ref}/branches` | `500` |
| GET | `/v1/projects/{ref}/branches/{name}` | `500` |
| **DELETE** | **`/v1/projects/{ref}/branches`** | **`401`, `403`, `429`, `500`** |

The last row is the tell: one endpoint in the same namespace already carries the
full set, so this reads as drift rather than an intentional contract.

The API does return those statuses. An invalid PAT against
`GET /v1/projects/{ref}/branches` — whose only documented failure is `500` —
returns a `401` with a structured body:

```console
$ curl -s -w '\nstatus=%{http_code}\n' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sbp_invalid' \
    https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/abcdefghijklmnopqrst/branches
{"message":"JWT could not be decoded"}
status=401
```

So a reader of https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-list-all-branches is told
the only way this call fails is a server error.

### 2. `GET /v1/branches/{id}/diff` requires `environment:write`, and the page doesn't say why

```
GET /v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/diff
  x-oauth-scope:      environment:write
  x-fga-permissions:  [[branching_development_write], [branching_production_write]]
```

This is the **only** `GET` operation in the entire v1 spec whose `x-oauth-scope`
ends in `:write`. The three other branching reads (`GET /v1/branches/{id}`,
`GET /v1/projects/{ref}/branches`, `GET /v1/projects/{ref}/branches/{name}`) all
use `environment:read`.

**I suspect this is deliberate**, and I'd rather name the likely reason than assume
a mistake: `V1DiffABranchParams` exposes a `pgdelta` toggle ("Use pg-delta instead
of Migra for diffing"), and both Migra and pg-delta compute a diff by provisioning a
shadow database and applying schema to it. If the endpoint does that server-side,
`:write` is the correct scope and the read/write split is working as designed.

Either way the docs don't say. An integrator building a read-only branch dashboard
reads the page, sees a `GET`, and has to request `environment:write` — which also
grants branch delete, reset, merge and push. Their end user's consent screen then
says the app can destroy branches, with no explanation available anywhere.
(Related appetite for finer-grained read scopes in #49702.)

## Describe the improvement

1. Add `401` / `403` / `429` to the 11 branching operations that omit them, matching
   `DELETE /v1/projects/{ref}/branches` and the other 151 operations in v1.
2. On `v1-diff-a-branch`, state why the scope is `environment:write` — or, if the
   scope is wider than the operation needs, narrow it to `environment:read`.

## Additional context

These pages are generated from the OpenAPI spec, which is also consumed for code
generation — including `packages/api`, the typed Management API client in the CLI
TypeScript rewrite. So the gap isn't only prose: generated clients model branching
failures as "`500` or a transport error", and a `401` from an expired PAT surfaces
as an unexpected response rather than an auth failure the caller can branch on.

Reproduction against the live spec:

```bash
curl -s https://api.supabase.com/api/v1-json -o spec.json
```

```python
import json
spec = json.load(open("spec.json"))
M = ("get", "post", "put", "patch", "delete")

# (1) error responses documented per branching operation
for path, item in sorted(spec["paths"].items()):
    if "branch" not in path:
        continue
    for method, op in item.items():
        if method in M:
            errs = sorted(c for c in op.get("responses", {}) if c[0] in "45")
            print(f"{method.upper():7}{path:44}{errs}")

# (2) the only GET in v1 requiring a :write scope
for path, item in spec["paths"].items():
    op = item.get("get")
    if op and str(op.get("x-oauth-scope", "")).endswith(":write"):
        print(path, "->", op["x-oauth-scope"])
```

Spec checked 2026-09-08: OpenAPI 3.0.0, 115 paths / 169 operations / 147 schemas.

One broader thing I left out because it isn't specific to branching: 580 of the 586
documented `4xx`/`5xx` responses across v1 carry no schema at all, so the
`{"message": ...}` body above isn't modelled anywhere and generated clients type
every error body as unknown. Happy to open that separately if it's usefull!

I'd be glad to open a PR for the response-documentation half if the spec is
generated from decorators in a repo that accepts external contributions, a pointer
would be welcome, since the generating source doesn't appear to be public.
items.title: API reference: 11 of 12 branching endpoints document only 500, and /diff is the only GET in v1 requiring a :write OAuth scope

## Description

When browsing the blog with a category filter selected, the first page is filtered correctly, but loading the next page loses the category parameter.

As a result, posts from other categories can be appended to the filtered list.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the blog page.
2. Select a category such as `postgres`.
3. Make sure the category has more than 25 posts.
4. Scroll to the bottom to trigger loading more posts.
5. Inspect the second request to `/api-v2/blog-posts`.

## Expected behavior

Every paginated request preserves the selected category:

`/api-v2/blog-posts?offset=25&limit=25&category=postgres`

## Actual behavior

The second request omits the category:

`/api-v2/blog-posts?offset=25&limit=25`

Posts from other categories are then appended to the current filtered list.

## Root cause

`handleFilterChange()` stores the selected category in `filterParams`, but `fetchMorePosts()` only adds `filterParams.search` to subsequent requests.

This behavior was introduced by the blog layout changes in #47236, which removed the existing category parameter from `fetchMorePosts()`.

## Proposed fix

Add the stored category to subsequent requests when it is not `all`.

Discovered a bug in `formatTableRowsToSQL`: schema, table, and column names are wrapped in double quotes but embedded double quotes are not escaped. PostgreSQL permits identifiers containing `"`, so Copy as SQL / Export as SQL can generate invalid SQL for valid table or column names.

Example table name: `customer"name` currently produces invalid SQL instead of quoting the identifier correctly.

A narrow fix is to escape `"` as `""` when quoting PostgreSQL identifiers and add regression coverage for schema/table/column names containing double quotes.

Clicking **Pricing** in the top nav from the homepage takes down the whole app. The page goes black and all that is left is:

> Application error: a client-side exception has occurred while loading supabase.com (see the browser console for more information).

Going to https://supabase.com/pricing directly works fine, so this only affects client-side navigation.

## Repro

1. Open https://supabase.com, hard reload so nothing comes from cache.
2. Wait around ten seconds, long enough for the `<Link>` prefetches to run.
3. Click **Pricing** in the nav.

Reproduced every time here, cold cache included.

## Console

The homepage starts logging these on its own, before I touch anything:

```
Failed to fetch RSC payload for https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api.
Falling back to browser navigation. ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk 4219 failed.
(error: .../www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/static/chunks/app/global-error-296163531e21ccae.js?dpl=dpl_2yThoLM9XXfiGovd3kDnKRrZfY6G)
```

Same for `/docs/guides/examples` and `/docs/guides/getting-started/quickstarts/reactjs`. Then clicking Pricing throws:

```
Uncaught ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk 2896 failed.
(error: https://frontend-assets.supabase.com/www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/static/chunks/2896-242ae3b31bc244ce.js?dpl=dpl_2yThoLM9XXfiGovd3kDnKRrZfY6G)
```

Two more requests come back 503 in the network panel:

```
GET /www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/static/chunks/app/guides/getting-started/[[...slug]]/page-bc5b37e1b87e8a6a.js?dpl=dpl_2yTho...
GET /www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/static/chunks/app/guides/getting-started/layout-138c9ce90351d9f3.js?dpl=dpl_2yTho...
```

## What I found

There are two Next apps on the same origin and they are on different deployments:

| | deployment | assets |
|---|---|---|
| www (`/`, `/pricing`) | `dpl_32HBeSJ1gP2wf4fRtd6rE336DoKu` | `/www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/...` |
| docs (`/docs/*`) | `dpl_2yThoLM9XXfiGovd3kDnKRrZfY6G` | `/docs/4ab1a6cbd220/_next/...` |

Since they share an origin, the www router treats the `/docs/...` links in the nav as internal routes and prefetches them. What comes back references chunk filenames from the docs build, but those get resolved against the www asset prefix, so the URL ends up half one build and half the other:

```
$ curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  'https://frontend-assets.supabase.com/www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/static/chunks/2896-242ae3b31bc244ce.js?dpl=dpl_2yThoLM9XXfiGovd3kDnKRrZfY6G'
404

$ curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  'https://frontend-assets.supabase.com/www/bf60e6cdcea1/_next/static/chunks/2896-5fe474d38512ff1d.js?dpl=dpl_32HBeSJ1gP2wf4fRtd6rE336DoKu'
200
```

Chunk 2896 in the www build is `5fe474d38512ff1d`, but the browser is asking for the docs build's `242ae3b31bc244ce`.

The failed prefetch by itself is harmless. The router falls back to a normal browser navigation and the docs links still work, which is probably why this went unnoticed for a while. The damage is that webpack caches the rejection for those chunk ids. 2896 is shared, so when the Pricing route asks for it the loader replays the cached failure, and the ChunkLoadError comes out of a click handler with nothing to catch it. The global-error chunk it falls through to is requested with the same wrong deployment id and 404s as well, which is why there is no error UI at all, just the black page.

## Possible fixes

Not sure which layer you would rather fix this at, but any one of these breaks the chain:

- `prefetch={false}` or a plain `<a>` on the docs links in the www nav, so the bad prefetch never happens
- keeping the two builds' chunk filenames from resolving against each other's asset prefix
- the `global-error` 404 seems worth a look on its own, since it turns any client-side error into a blank page

## Environment

Chrome 152 on macOS 26.6 (Apple silicon), served from `fra1`. Seen on 2026-09-01 with www `dpl_32HBeSJ1gP2wf4fRtd6rE336DoKu` and docs `dpl_2yThoLM9XXfiGovd3kDnKRrZfY6G`.

# Query builder generates invalid SQL for empty `in` filters

## Bug

Passing an empty array to an `in` filter generates PostgreSQL syntax such as:

```sql
select * from public.users where id in ();
```

PostgreSQL rejects `IN ()` with a syntax error. Tuple filters have the same problem:

```sql
where (id, version) in ()
```

## Reproduction

```ts
new Query()
  .from('users', 'public')
  .select()
  .filter('id', 'in', [])
  .toSql()
```

This is reachable in Studio's vault helpers. `getDecryptedParameters()` passes `Object.values(paramsToBeDecrypted)` to `getDecryptedValues()`. For wrappers with no encrypted parameters, that value is an empty array and the generated vault query is invalid.

## Expected

Membership in an empty set should produce a valid always-false predicate, so selects return no rows and updates or deletes remain safe no-ops.

## Bug

The Table Editor shows the wrong row count when a number column is filtered by `0`.

The rows themselves are filtered correctly, but the count still reflects the full table. For example, if a table has 100 rows and only 8 have `quantity = 0`, the grid shows those 8 rows while the count can still show 100.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a table with a number column containing both zero and non-zero values.
2. Add an `equals` filter for that column.
3. Enter `0` and apply the filter.
4. Compare the visible rows with the row count.

## Expected

The count should use the same filter as the rows.

## What is happening

Studio converts the input string `"0"` to the number `0` before building the count query. The count query then checks the value by truthiness, so it treats `0` as if no value was provided and leaves the filter out.

Blank filter values need to remain ignored, since converting an empty string with `Number('')` also produces `0`.

## Summary

`pgMeta.tables.update` (when `primary_keys` is supplied) and `pgMeta.columns.update`
(the `is_unique: false` and `check: ...` paths) all build `DO $$ ... $$;` blocks
whose body embeds `old.schema` / `old.name` / `old.table` via `ident()` inside
strings that are then passed to `EXECUTE` or to `format()`. When any of those
identifiers happens to contain the literal byte sequence `$$`, PostgreSQL's
dollar-quote parser treats the first `$$` it sees in the body as the closing
delimiter of the outer block, the body is parsed as truncated, and the
statement fails with a `syntax error at or near "..."` error.

This is the same class of bug as the recently-opened `pg-meta-table-privileges`
(#49523), `pg-meta-column-privileges` (#49588), `pg-meta-roles` (#49600),
`pg-meta-foreign-tables` (#49603), and `pg-meta-publications` (#49605) PRs —
those five paths already use a collision-free `getDoBlockDelimiter(...)` helper.
The same pattern still exists in two files: `pg-meta-tables.ts` (PK drop block)
and `pg-meta-columns.ts` (UNIQUE drop block and CHECK replace block).

## Repro

```sql
create table public."weird$$name" (id int primary key, val text);
-- what pgMeta.tables.update({...name: 'weird$$name'...}, { primary_keys: [] })
-- generates on master today:
do $$
declare r record;
begin
  select conname into r from pg_constraint
    where contype = 'p' and conrelid = 1;
  if r is not null then
    execute 'ALTER TABLE public."weird$$name" DROP CONSTRAINT ' || quote_ident(r.conname);
  end if;
end
$$;
-- ERROR:  syntax error at or near "name"
```

The outer `$$` closes at the `$$` inside `"weird$$name"`, the body after that
is parsed as the next statement, and the EXECUTE argument (which started with
the literal text `ALTER TABLE public."weird$$name"`) is truncated at the first
inner `$$`. PostgreSQL then chokes on the partial token.

The same breakage applies to:
- `pgMeta.columns.update(col, { is_unique: false })` for a column on a table
  whose name contains `$$` (the UNIQUE-drop DO block in
  `pg-meta-columns.ts:303`).
- `pgMeta.columns.update(col, { check: ... })` for a column on a table whose
  name or schema contains `$$` (the CHECK-replace DO block in
  `pg-meta-columns.ts:340`, which embeds schema/table inside a `format(...)`
  call).

## Expected

The DO block should pick a delimiter that is absent from every value that
flows into the body, just like the five sibling fixes already do. A table
named `weird$$name` should round-trip cleanly through
`pgMeta.tables.update({...}, { primary_keys: [] })` and through the column
update paths, and the same for any schema or column name that contains
`$$`.

## Suggested fix

Introduce a `getDoBlockDelimiter(values: string[])` helper in each of
`pg-meta-tables.ts` and `pg-meta-columns.ts` (mirroring the helpers already
shipped in the sibling files) and substitute its return value for the literal
`$$` opener / closer in the three DO blocks listed above. For the PK path,
`values = [old.schema, old.name]`; for the UNIQUE path,
`values = [old.schema, old.table]`; for the CHECK path,
`values = [old.schema, old.table, old.name]`.

I'm happy to send a PR with regression tests covering the three paths plus a

# Improve documentation

## Link 

[https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/connect-to-postgres#using-drizzle](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/connect-to-postgres#using-drizzle)

## Describe the problem

The [docs for using drizzle in an edge function](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/connect-to-postgres#using-drizzle) contain a misleading comment in their code example. 

```typescript
const connectionString = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_DB_URL')!
// Disable prefetch as it is not supported for "Transaction" pool mode
const client = postgres(connectionString, { prepare: false })
```

As the example currently is, it suggests that `SUPABASE_DB_URL` is a url that pools connections and does not support prefetching prepared statements. In reality it is a non-pooling direct connection.

## Describe the improvement

The docs should not mislead developers into thinking that their connections to `SUPABASE_DB_URL` will be pooled by the server.

```typescript
// Get a direct connection string. In production Edge Functions, it's recommended
// to connect via the transaction pooler URL by adding it as a secret.
const connectionString = Deno.env.get('SUPABASE_DB_URL')!

// Prepared statements are disabled so this works with the transaction pooler,
// which doesn't support them.
const client = postgres(connectionString, { prepare: false })
```

## Additional context

I ran into this issue myself after deploying an edge function. I followed the examples when building my function and started seeing this error in the logs once deployed: `remaining connection slots are reserved for roles with the SUPERUSER attribute`. I resolved it by switching to a transaction pooler url. 

I'll open an PR shortly to resolve the documentation issue.

## Root Cause
I investigated the codebase and found three distinct issues across two different files:

1. **CSS Selector Bug in `apps/learn/app/(app)/page.tsx`**:
   In the `Home` component, the code renders 13 vertical grid lines in a loop and attempts to hide the first and last lines using Tailwind's `first:hidden last:hidden` classes. However, the parent container also contains the "Grid Content" `div` as a sibling immediately after the mapped grid lines. Because this content `div` is the actual last child of the parent container, the CSS `:last-child` selector (which Tailwind's `last:` compiles to) targets the content `div` instead of the 13th grid line. This leaves the 13th grid line visible.

2. **Stale Input Value in `apps/lite-studio/app/routes/projects.$ref.tsx`**:
   In the `ProjectPage` component, the project name input field uses `defaultValue={ref}`. In React, `defaultValue` only sets the input's value on the initial mount. If a user switches projects (which changes the `ref` route parameter), the input field will not update to show the new project name because React does not re-mount the component.

3. **Uncleared Timeout in `apps/lite-studio/app/routes/projects.$ref.tsx`**:
   Also in the `ProjectPage` component, the "Refresh Status" button's `onClick` handler triggers a 2-second timeout to toggle the `loading` state back to `false`. This timer is never cleared. If the user navigates away or unmounts the component before the 2 seconds are up, React will attempt to update the state of an unmounted component, which triggers a memory leak warning.

## Evidence
* **`apps/learn/app/(app)/page.tsx`**: 
  I confirmed this by reading the `Home` component directly. The vertical grid lines are mapped inside a `relative` container, followed immediately by the "Grid Content" `div`. This structure breaks the `:last-child` CSS assumption.
* **`apps/lite-studio/app/routes/projects.$ref.tsx`**: 
  I confirmed this by reading the `ProjectPage` component directly. The `onClick` handler uses `setTimeout(() => setLoading(false), 2000)` without saving or clearing the timeout ID. The project name input uses `defaultValue={ref}` without a key to force re-renders on route changes.

## Suggested Fix
* **For the grid lines in `apps/learn/app/(app)/page.tsx`**:
  Avoid relying on CSS `:last-child`. Instead, use the loop index to conditionally apply the hidden class:
  ```tsx
  className={`absolute top-0 bottom-0 w-px bg-border/30 z-10 ${i === 0 || i === 12 ? 'hidden' : ''}`}
  ```
* **For the project name input in `apps/lite-studio/app/routes/projects.$ref.tsx`**:
  Add `key={ref}` to the `<Input>` element. This forces React to destroy and recreate the input with the correct default value whenever the project changes:
  ```tsx
  <Input key={ref} id="project-name" placeholder="my-project" defaultValue={ref} />
  ```
* **For the timeout in `apps/lite-studio/app/routes/projects.$ref.tsx`**:
  Manage the timer inside a `useEffect` hook or store the timeout ID in a React `useRef` so that you can clear it in a cleanup function when the component unmounts.

## Confidence & Gaps
I am highly confident in these findings as I confirmed them by reading the code directly. 

We also found theme files like `apps/design-system/lib/themes/supabase-2.json` and `apps/learn/lib/themes/supabase-2.json` during our search. However, these are static configuration files for code highlighting and do not impact application logic, so they are not relevant to these bugs.

The registry schema currently defines `backendProviders` as an array of arbitrary strings:

```ts
backendProviders: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
```

However, the same file defines a list of supported backend providers:

```ts
const backendProviderValues = ['next-auth', 'supabase', 'auth0']
```

```ts
const backendProviderValues = ['next-auth', 'supabase', 'auth0'] as const

backendProviders: z.array(z.enum(backendProviderValues)).optional(),
```

## Summary

Creating a preview branch produces a database whose **schema** matches its parent but whose **privileges and
`auth`-schema triggers do not**. Two distinct losses, measured, reproducible on every branch we create:

1. **Object privileges are not preserved.** `GRANT`/`REVOKE` state on `public` functions and tables is
   replaced by what the schema's default privileges produce, so roles hold access the parent revoked.
2. **Triggers on `auth.users` are not created.** A trigger the parent carries is simply absent.

The first is a security-relevant divergence: on our branches `anon` holds every privilege on tables the parent
revokes it from, and `authenticated` can execute functions the parent restricts to `service_role`.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Branch created via | `POST /v1/branches` (Management API), `with_data: false` |
| Instance size | `ci_micro` |
| PostgreSQL | 17.6 |
| Schema size | 285 migrations · 385 `public` functions · 98 `public` tables · 118 RLS policies |

## Defect 1 — object privileges are not preserved

### Expected

A branch's `public` objects carry the same `relacl` / `proacl` as the parent's.

### Actual

They carry what the schema's default privileges produce. Measured on a fresh branch, comparing raw ACLs:

| object class | rows compared | differ from parent |
|---|---|---|
| function ACLs | 385 | **204** |
| table ACLs | 98 | **45** |

Representative examples — parent first, branch second:

```
activate_tenant(uuid)
  parent: postgres=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres
  branch: postgres=X/postgres, anon=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres

contacts
  parent: postgres=arwdDxtm, authenticated=arwdDxtm, service_role=arwdDxtm
  branch: … plus anon=arwdDxtm          ← every privilege, on a table the parent revokes anon from

call_disposition_catalog
  parent: authenticated=r               ← read only
  branch: authenticated=arwdDxtm        ← full write
```

### What IS preserved

Worth stating, because it narrows the cause: **row-level security is intact.** Comparing parent to branch:

| dimension | differences |
|---|---|
| RLS enabled / forced | **0** |
| RLS policies (118) | **0** |
| schema `USAGE` on `public` | **0** |
| sequence ACLs | **0** |
| default ACLs in `public` | **0** |

So policies survive; the grants beneath them do not. Where RLS also applies, table access still narrows by
tenant — but **functions have no RLS**, so for functions the loss is unmitigated.

### Likely mechanism

Consistent with objects being **recreated as `postgres`** during branch provisioning, allowing `public`'s
default privileges to apply, with the parent's explicit `GRANT`/`REVOKE` state not replayed afterwards.

⚠ Two candidate causes we **ruled out by measurement**, in case they save you time:

- **It is not `PUBLIC`.** The raw ACLs name `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly, granted by `postgres`.
- **It is not a default-ACL difference in `public`.** Those are identical between parent and branch (24 rows
  each). The branch has **three extra** `pg_default_acl` rows, all in the **`supabase_functions`** schema,
  which appear to be ordinary platform provisioning and unrelated.

## Defect 2 — triggers on `auth.users` are not created

### Expected

A trigger the parent has on `auth.users` exists on the branch.

### Actual

It is absent.

```
auth-schema triggers    parent: 1    branch: 0
  parent has, branch lacks:
    users :: on_auth_user_created -> handle_new_user (AFTER INSERT, enabled=O)
```

The trigger is created by one of our migrations:

```sql
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function handle_new_user();
```

### Impact

Signup does not produce the row the trigger exists to create, so any test of post-signup behaviour fails on a
branch while passing against the parent. This is the failure that led us to look: an end-to-end test asserting
that a profile row appears after `auth.admin.createUser` returns **PGRST116 — "The result contains 0 rows"**.

## Reproduction

1. On a project with non-default grants in `public` and a trigger on `auth.users`, create a branch:
   `POST /v1/branches` with `with_data: false`.
2. Wait for the branch to reach a settled state. ⚠ `ACTIVE_HEALTHY` is **not** terminal — we observe
   `… → ACTIVE_HEALTHY → RESTORING → ACTIVE_HEALTHY`, and reading at the first one returns zeros.
3. Connect to the branch and to the parent, and compare:

```sql
-- privileges (run against both, then diff)
select p.oid::regprocedure::text, coalesce(array_to_string(p.proacl::text[], ','), 'NULL')
  from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
 where n.nspname = 'public' and p.prokind = 'f' order by 1;

select c.relname, coalesce(array_to_string(c.relacl::text[], ','), 'NULL')
  from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
 where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relkind = 'r' order by 1;

-- auth triggers (run against both)
select c.relname, t.tgname, p.proname
  from pg_trigger t
  join pg_class c on c.oid = t.tgrelid
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
  join pg_proc p on p.oid = t.tgfoid
 where n.nspname = 'auth' and not t.tgisinternal;
```

Both differences appear on every branch we have created. **Neither is intermittent**: the privilege figures
(204 / 45) were identical across four separate branches, and the missing trigger reproduced on every run.

## What we are doing meanwhile

Reconciling privileges after branch creation, from a schema built out of our own migrations. It works — it
took an end-to-end suite from 21 of 33 passing to 30 of 33 — but it is a workaround for something we would
rather not have to detect.

We have **not** recreated the `auth` trigger on a branch. Not because we believe it unsafe: our own migration
creates exactly that trigger on three ordinary projects, and the
[User Management guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data) documents the same pattern.
It is that a branch's schema does not appear to come from replaying our migrations, so the migration that
creates the trigger never runs there — which is what question 2 below is really asking about.

## Questions

**1. Is privilege loss on branch creation known, or expected behaviour we should design around?**

The closest statement we can find in the docs is
[Branching via the dashboard → Limitations](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/branching/dashboard#limitations):

> Custom roles created through the dashboard are not captured on branch creation

That is about **roles**. What we lose is **grants to the three built-in roles** — `anon`, `authenticated`,
`service_role` — on objects our own migrations create. If those are the same underlying behaviour, the
limitation as written is far narrower than what it covers.

**2. How is a branch's schema actually produced?**

The same Limitations list says:

> If you have run migrations on main, new branches will be created from existing migrations instead of a full
> schema dump

We have run migrations on main. On that description the branch is built by replaying them — and the migration
quoted under Defect 2 creates `on_auth_user_created`. It is not on the branch. Meanwhile the branch **does**
have all 385 functions and 98 tables those same migrations create, so the schema is reproduced somehow.

So one of these should be true, and which one decides whether Defect 2 shares a root cause with Defect 1:

- that statement describes dashboard branching only, and Management-API branches are produced another way;
- the replay happens but skips DDL targeting the `auth` schema;
- the replay happens as a role without `TRIGGER` on `auth.users`, and that one failure is swallowed.

The third would account for both defects at once — the branch being built by a role with different authority
than the parent's owner.

---

*Edited 2026-08-22: a third question — whether recreating a trigger on `auth.users` is safe — was removed. The
User Management guide documents that pattern, and we already do it on three non-branch projects, so it was not
ours to ask. Question 2 was rewritten to state the contradiction with the documented branch-creation mechanism
rather than to ask an open-ended "same root cause?".*

[Securing your API](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api) gives four `alter default privileges` statements so new objects are not exposed. The last one has no effect. Functions created afterwards are still callable with the anon key.

## Repro

Safe to paste into the SQL editor. It rolls back and changes nothing.

```sql
begin;

-- the four statements from the docs, verbatim
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public
  revoke select, insert, update, delete on tables from anon, authenticated, service_role;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public
  revoke execute on functions from anon, authenticated, service_role;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public
  revoke usage, select on sequences from anon, authenticated, service_role;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public
  revoke execute on functions from public;

create function public.after_docs() returns int language sql as 'select 1';
create table public.after_docs_t (id int);

select 'function' as obj, has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') as anon_access
from pg_proc where proname = 'after_docs'
union all
select 'table', has_table_privilege('anon', oid, 'SELECT')
from pg_class where relname = 'after_docs_t';

rollback;
```

```
   obj    | anon_access
----------+-------------
 function | true
 table    | false
```

The table is protected. The function is not. Its `proacl` comes back null, so it falls back to the built-in default, which grants EXECUTE to `PUBLIC`, and `anon` inherits that.

## Cause

An `IN SCHEMA` default ACL is merged with the built-in default instead of replacing it. It can add privileges, but it cannot remove one the built-in default supplies. The schema-less form replaces the built-in default, so the revoke sticks there.

Tables are unaffected because their built-in default grants nothing to `PUBLIC`. That is why the other three statements work and this one is easy to miss.

## Fix

Drop `in schema public` from that statement:

```sql
alter default privileges for role postgres
  revoke execute on functions from public;
```

The same function then comes out as `{postgres=X/postgres}` and `anon` cannot execute it.

## Impact

This is the security hardening page. Every statement succeeds, so you can reasonably believe new functions are limited to your backend while anyone holding your anon key can still call them. We hit this on a production project, where a `security definer` function reading from `auth.users` stayed publicly callable long after the hardening was applied.

# Bug report

- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application.
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [[Docs](https://docs.supabase.com/)](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [[Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions)](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [[Discord](https://discord.supabase.com/)](https://discord.supabase.com).

## Describe the bug

Branching webhooks (`--notify-url`) cannot target an Edge Function hosted on a **different** Supabase project. The webhook request is sent with an `apikey` header containing the **source** project's publishable key. When the notify URL points to an Edge Function on another project (a dedicated "DevOps" project), that project's API gateway rejects the request with `401 UNAUTHORIZED_INVALID_API_KEY` — because the key belongs to the source project, not the target one. The Edge Function code never executes.

This makes it impossible to decouple product projects from a central DevOps/observability project when consuming branching events.

## To Reproduce

1. Have two Supabase projects: `MAIN` (product, with branching enabled) and `DEVOPS`.
2. Deploy an Edge Function on `DEVOPS`, e.g. `notify-slack`.
3. Configure the branching webhook on `MAIN`:
   ```bash
   supabase branches update main --notify-url https://<DEVOPS_PROJECT_REF>.supabase.co/functions/v1/notify-slack
   ```
4. Trigger a branching event (e.g. push to a branch / merge to main).
5. Inspect the Edge Function logs on `DEVOPS`: the request never reaches the function.

Observed in the request/response logs:

Request header injected by the webhook (source project's key):
```json
"request.sb.apikey.apikey.prefix": "sb_publishable_$MAIN_PROJECT_PUBLISHABLE_KEY"
```

Response from the `DEVOPS` gateway:
```json
"response.headers.sb_error_code": "UNAUTHORIZED_INVALID_API_KEY"
```

## Expected behavior

One of:
- The branching webhook should not inject the source project's `apikey` header when the notify URL is not the source project itself (it's an arbitrary external URL, potentially another Supabase project); or
- There should be a way to configure the auth headers sent with the webhook (custom header / shared secret), similar to Database Webhooks; or
- The target project's gateway should allow the request to reach the function when JWT verification is disabled, instead of hard-rejecting on a foreign `apikey` header.

Any of these would allow receiving branching webhooks on a separate project to decouple product and DevOps concerns.

## Screenshots

N/A — relevant log excerpts included above.

## System information

- running on Supabase hosted

## Additional context

- The 401 is returned by the target project's API gateway, before the Edge Function runtime — so function-level workarounds (e.g. handling auth inside the function) are not applicable.
- Use case: a central "DevOps" project aggregating branching lifecycle events from multiple product projects (Slack notifications, CI orchestration). Currently the only workaround is hosting the receiver on the same project or on non-Supabase infrastructure, which defeats the purpose of consolidating on Supabase.

In the Table Editor, "Copy rows as SQL" and "Export table as SQL" (both go through `formatTableRowsToSQL` in `apps/studio/components/interfaces/TableGridEditor/TableEntity.utils.ts`) generate broken SQL for json/jsonb columns.

The json branch does:

```
JSON.stringify(val).replace(/\\"/g, '"').replace(/'/g, "''").replace('"', "'").replace(/.$/, "'")
```

Two problems:

- A json value with a double quote inside a string (e.g. `{"note": "say \"hi\""}`) produces invalid SQL. Reimporting it fails with `invalid input syntax for type json`.
- A json value with a backslash (a Windows path, a `\n`, a `\uXXXX`, a regex) gets every backslash doubled, so the restored value silently differs from the original.

Since this is a backup/migration feature, both are bad: one breaks the export outright, the other corrupts data quietly.

Repro:

```sql
create table demo (id int, metadata jsonb);
insert into demo values
  (1, jsonb_build_object('note', 'say "hi"')),
  (2, jsonb_build_object('path', 'C:\Users\me'));
```

Select the two rows in the Table Editor and Copy as SQL. The generated INSERT for row 1 is invalid JSON (won't run), and row 2 comes out with `C:\\\\Users\\\\me` instead of `C:\\Users\\me`.

The text/varchar branch a few lines down already does the right thing (`'${val.replaceAll("'", "''")}'`). The json value just needs the same single-quote escaping; it already arrives as JSON text (or an object that should be stringified first).

When you import rows (CSV upload or spreadsheet paste) into a table that has an identity or serial column, Studio runs a "raise the sequence" step afterwards so the sequence continues above the imported values. That step uses `getUpdateIdentitySequenceSQL` (`packages/pg-meta/src/sql/studio/table-editor/identity.ts`), which builds the first argument to `pg_get_serial_sequence` like this:

```
pg_get_serial_sequence('<schema>.<table>', '<column>')
```

The schema and table are joined without quoting. `pg_get_serial_sequence` reads an unquoted argument as a case-folded identifier, so for a table or schema whose name has uppercase letters (e.g. `Users`, common for people coming from Prisma or TypeORM) it looks for `schema.users` and errors with `relation "..." does not exist`.

Two consequences:

1. The import surfaces a database error even though the rows already landed.
2. The sequence is never raised, so it stays at 1. The next insert that relies on the identity/serial default generates 1, 2, 3... which collide with the imported rows and fail with a duplicate primary key.

Repro:

```sql
create schema "App";
create table "App"."Users" ("Id" bigint generated by default as identity primary key, val text);
insert into "App"."Users" ("Id", val) values (5, 'a'), (6, 'b');

-- what the builder currently generates:
select pg_get_serial_sequence('App.Users', 'Id');
-- ERROR:  relation "app.users" does not exist
```

The same function already quotes the relation correctly in its `FROM` clause, and the sibling `getDuplicateIdentitySequenceSQL` quotes its `::regclass` argument with `ident()`. Only the `pg_get_serial_sequence` argument was left unquoted.

Dropdown has no internal scrollbar, so Apply button is inaccessible ## Expected behavior Dropdown should either reposition itself above the trigger when there's insufficient space below, or have an internal scroll so all options + Apply button remain reachable ## Screenshots If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem. ## System information - OS: Windows - Browser: Chrome - Version of supabase-js: N/A — this bug is in the Supabase Dashboard (web app), not the client library - Version of Node.js: N/A — issue reproduced directly in-browser, no local project involved - Dashboard URL: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/vkwefjpfuzlpopdocdgm/functions/process-reminder-notifications/logs ## Additional context I found this issue in multiple locations across the dashboard, all sharing the same underlying dropdown implementation (`data-radix-popper-content-wrapper` — Radix UI's Popper component): 1. **Edge Function Logs → Severity filter dropdown**: gets clipped by the viewport at reduced window heights, with no way to reach the Apply button. 2. **Table Editor → Add foreign key relationship → "Select columns from [table]" dropdown**: flips to open upward when space below is limited, but topmost items remain clipped above the viewport. 3. Even the "Select a table to reference to" dropdown in the same modal, which initially appeared to scroll correctly, also has its lower portion clipped under certain conditions. Since all of these use the same `data-radix-popper-content-wrapper`, this points to a single root cause rather than isolated bugs per-dropdown — likely the Popper's collision boundary / available-height calculation isn't correctly clamping the content to the visible viewport in all cases, so the internal scroll area is sized larger than what's actually reachable on screen. Zooming out the browser (or resizing the window / opening Chrome DevTools, which changes the effective viewport) reveals the full modal content that was previously clipped, confirming this is a positioning/sizing issue rather than missing content — the dropdown's available-height calculation isn't correctly accounting for the actual visible viewport at normal zoom/window sizes. Below: the same " Severity filter dropdown" modal at reduced browser zoom, showing all dropdown options and buttons fully visible and reachable.
